title: First bands: Pellis Band and Cornish's band
summary: The six-piece Pellis Band was his first real band; he then joined Cornish's band on sax and played with Jack Carey.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Lorenzo, yeah. Well, by that time I had got to playing pretty good. Then I went and played with, we made up another band, Pellis Band. That was the first real band we made up, you know? And we played Rania and made pretty good hits.
Who was with you in the Pellis Band?

Pellis Band, well at that time we had Nyash Ross on bass. And Alan Gordett on trumpet. I was on clarinet. I can't remember who was playing guitar and drums. But I know that was our first little band, you know? About how many pieces were it? We had six. Six pieces. Six pieces, yeah. Then I, after people found out I could play well, then we started splitting up and getting with different bands. I played with Willie Cornish. I had me and Willie Cornish on trombone. And Octave Crosby on drums. And Sam Toole's on banjo. Oh dear He had a son named Nat Toad. Oh sure, yeah. He's called W-L-E-S. Yeah, his son's a bass player. Sure, yeah. There was a whole family of musicians. I never did know any of them.
I've seen the name and the picture of their band.

Yeah, well I played with them and then Sam and Cornish got in a little misunderstanding and he split up. And Cornish made up his own band, well I went with Cornish. And I left off a clarinet then and went on sax, and John went in the band on clarinet. Cornish was on trombone and we had Wood and Joe playing Cornish. That was the lineup, you know, in that band. And I played with him a while. And finally Jack Kerris band made a split. And at that time his name was Fame around here, you know. Yeah, her mother, Punchy told us about him. Yeah, well his band split up and I think that was when Punchy first decided to go off. Went off of the show or something like that. Well anyway Jack Kerris taught me and my brother-in-law to join the band. We was young kids and we just wanted to have that name or saying we played with Jack Kerris, you know. So we joined the band and made out pretty good with the exception that he used to cheat us out of our money when we were knocked off. We'd play the jobs and they'd pay us short, you know. Tell us to go around and tell everybody we was playing with Jack Kerris. Well we thought that was a big honor. And we played with Jack for I guess about a year going on just letting him play us and take our money, just glad to be with the band. Him and Willigan. Willigan was his drum player at that time. You heard of Willigan, eh? Jim Willigan? Yeah. What was his name?

He never knew. Well he's one of the old drummers around here. He died long years ago. Well we played on with Jack until finally we started learning a little more about the music again and started getting off again, you know. At that time, I mean the older musicians was always trying to take advantage of the young musicians. They never wanted to treat them fat, you see. So then I got a chance then to switch and play with different bands. I played with Buddy Petit and I played with Chris Kelly for a while. And we decided to make a brass band.
